author: reek
body: TrackerApp's project sidebar is a TreeView, and ItemDesignerApp, CallPage and diagram's Toolbar each build one. None of them had a test.

author: reek
body: The chapter divides cleanly into what the one live caller reaches and what it does not. TrackerApp builds a tree and renders it, so construction, depth assignment, the flatten and the widget rows are live. Expanding, selecting and navigating are reached by nothing, which is exactly why they are asked here: a function nobody calls that is wrong is a trap laid for its first caller, and this chapter's whole purpose is that a tree can be opened.

author: reek
body: The tree below is three levels deep on one branch and one level on another, so a flatten that returned everything and a flatten that honoured the expanded flags are visibly different, and so are pre-order and any other order.

author: reek
body: a has two children; a-1 itself has a child. b is a leaf. c has one child.

author: reek
body: Depth is assigned at construction and every row's indent is computed from it, so it is read at all three levels rather than at the roots only.

author: reek
body: Toggling a node whose parent is shut must still flip the node, or opening the parent afterwards shows it shut.

author: reek
body: Selecting a second node must leave exactly one selected, or every click adds another and nothing ever deselects.

target: section:What a caller still holding the tree sees
author: reek
body: Both of these hand back a state, so a caller holding the one it passed in must find it as it left it.

author: reek
body: The original is read AFTER the call, never before: a snapshot taken first records what the tree was and can never disagree with itself.

author: reek
body: And the whole tree is walked, not the roots: the node under test is two levels down, so a top-level scan reports nothing selected whatever happened.

author: reek
body: A fresh tree has no focus. The first Down keypress is therefore the case that matters most and the one a test written from the middle of a session never reaches.

author: reek
body: The parent walk is reached from `tv-collapse-or-parent` only for a node that was found, so a missing focus cannot arrive through that door. It is a published name and a citing chapter can call it, so it is called here with a tree that has no focus at all.

author: reek
body: This line pins the ANSWER and not the guard, and the difference is worth being plain about: deleting the bounds check in `tv-go-parent` does not move this line, because the parent search refuses a start of -1 by itself. The guard exists to stop the read that happens first, which would take `list-at` one below element zero and land on the list's capacity cell. Nothing this harness can print distinguishes the two, and saying so here is better than leaving a guard that looks tested.

author: reek
body: A fresh tree renders its roots and nothing else, which is what the one live caller shows. Each row is an indent, an expander, an icon and a label, so the expander glyph is what says whether a branch can be opened.
